INDEPENDENT OPM · 0.11b · 2026-09-16

YM2151 LFO — from recordings to equations

Trace the recordings, equations and implementation limits in one report.

TimingDepthRandomLimitsAll recordings

What this report demonstrates

This report describes the current independent-opm 0.11b implementation. It separates measurements, fitted models and implementation approximations. All 41 LFO recordings have an overview and a magnified actual audio waveform.

314,361AM comparison points; zero half-step errors
4,153held-out 42STATE steps; zero mismatches
160,934held-out random-AM bits; zero errors

“Evidence” here means agreement over finite observations. It does not establish a unique physical circuit, perfect reproduction of every register sequence, or legal independence.

1. What is extracted from the audio

The supplied setup is 4 MHz, G.I.M.I.C optical digital output, 96 kHz / 24-bit stereo. Recordings 37–42 compare the modulated left channel with the reference right channel. The audio carrier and its slowly changing LFO modulation are different quantities.

AM(t) = −20 log10(Aleft(t) / Aright(t))  [dB]
PM(t) = 1200 log2(fleft(t) / fright(t))  [cent]

Amplitude and phase derivative are extracted from the native 96 kHz analytic signal, then averaged in 1 ms bins. PM comparisons also use a five-point median filter. Formal comparisons omit initial transients and ±4 ms around steps. A separate sinusoidal/harmonic fit checked 36 native 8 ms excerpts in 37/39/41. Digital capture after SRC is not direct access to the chip’s internal bits.

2. Timing equations

F = register 18h; H = F >> 4; L = F & 15
Tbase = 2^(24−H) master clocks
Nnative = 2^(18−H) samples  (native sample = 64 clocks)
r(n) = reverse4(n mod 16)
increment(n) = 1 + [r(n) < L]
p ← (p + increment × (triangle ? 2 : 1)) mod 512

reverse4 reverses four bits, producing 0,8,4,12,2,10,6,14,1,9,5,13,3,11,7,15. The low nibble controls which updates advance two positions. An ordinary fractional accumulator can match the average yet produce a different order.

Average period = 256 × 2^(24−H) / (master_clock × (1 + L/16))
F=80h, 4 MHz: 4.194304 s
F=FFh, 4 MHz: ≈0.0169125 s; base update every 8 native samples

Complete measurement intervals for all 256 settings were obtained after 25R1–R3. This is coverage, not identification of every internal step sequence. At 00h–1Fh, 832 held-out steps matched, including 260 predicted in new recordings. For 42STATE, 96 trials at 81h/87h/8Fh used the first 16 steps to estimate phase and compared the remaining 4,153 steps.

42STATE candidateHeld-out mismatches
Four-bit reversal0 / 4,153
Simple fractional accumulation516 / 4,153

Measured step example: 42STATE / FREQ=87h

━ Measured change

These are stored detected changes divided by the attenuation unit, not raw sine samples. Steps near one and two units appear. The reproducibility package includes all 96 trials and candidate mismatch counts.

3. Waveform values

p = position & 511; u = p & 255; d = p & 127
Saw:     AM = 255−u; PM = (u<128 ? u : u−255)
Square:  AM = (u<128 ? 255 : 0); PM = (u<128 ? 128 : −128)
Triangle AM = (p<256 ? 255−p : p−256)
Triangle PM, quarter p>>7:
  0: d    1: 127−d    2: −d    3: d−127

Triangle advances the shared position by two, giving 256 observed positions in steady operation. Odd positions reached after waveform changes are an interpolation policy, not fully measured endpoints.

4. Depth arithmetic

a = floor(AM × AMD / 128)
AM_dB = AMS==0 ? 0 : a × 2^(AMS−1) × 0.0940893095546545
m = floor(abs(PM) × PMD / 128)
PMS=0: q=0
PMS=1..5: |q| = m >> (6−PMS)
PMS=6..7: |q| = m << (PMS−5)
sign(q) = sign(PM)
Current core: pitch displacement ≈ q × 100/64 cent

AM was tested for three waveforms and all 128 AMD values at AMS1. The dB coefficient is an acoustic calibration from even-AMD square levels. AMS2/3 scaling and deep-AM rounding remain approximate. PM truncates the magnitude and restores its sign; this differs from directly right-shifting a negative number.

RecordingPointsMedian section RMSMaximum section RMS
37104,7630.001995 dB0.002200 dB
38104,7720.001899 dB0.004343 dB
39104,8260.001742 dB0.002025 dB
40173,5670.150775 cent0.200151 cent
41242,2830.154807 cent0.204478 cent

AM phase was fitted in the first 4.05 seconds of each section; 4.3–5.9 seconds were compared. All 314,361 points were within half an attenuation unit. Correlated 1 ms observations are not independent internal bits.

The PM errors use integer q with an empirical pitch-response table calibrated on part of recording 40. They are not errors of the current core’s q×100/64-cent conversion. Tests cover 16 selected PMD values, all eight PMS values and one carrier pitch. Thirty-two points in 41 lacked a calibration entry and were excluded. The rejected −128-start candidate gave maximum RMS errors of 2.828 and 3.777 cents; −127 matched better.

5. Random sequence: inference without preset degree

The attenuation from 08LONG was binarized using 255 candidate thresholds. A GF(2) linear recurrence was inferred from the first 512 bits without prescribing its degree or taps. The selected threshold was about 11.919297 dB; the inferred degree was 17 with lags 14 and 17.

b[n] = b[n−14] XOR b[n−17]

One equivalent state encoding (0 ≤ s < 2^17):
step(s) = ((s >> 1) | (((s XOR (s >> 3)) & 1) << 16)) & 0x1FFFF

16 updates in one expression:
q = s XOR (s >> 3)
advance16(s) = (s >> 16) XOR (((q << 1) XOR (q << 15)) & 0x1FFFF)

There were zero errors on the remaining 160,934 bits and on 311,631 held-out bits from seven noise conditions. The analysis accounts for 1,611 missing updates inferred from timestamps; the capture is not a gap-free raw bit stream. The closed-form 16-step update was equivalent to 16 single steps for all 131,072 states.

Minimality concerns the degree of a GF(2) linear recurrence for the examined sequence. It does not prove the fewest instructions among all possible programs or a physical 17-stage register. The current sequence_advance16 is a table-free, loop-free equivalent calculation.

08LONG: measured attenuation and binarization threshold

━ Stored measured attenuation ━ Threshold

The figure shows 128 points following the first 512 training points. Binarizing attenuation and reconstructing the eight-bit AM value are separate validation stages.

Example of held-out bit prediction

━ Binarized recording ━ Recurrence prediction

The two lines coincide at all 128 points. Prediction is not updated with measured bits after the first 512 points.

6. Random advancement and eight-bit capture

Dnoise = 32 × (32 − (NFRQ & 31)) master clocks
Every Dnoise: state ← advance16(state)
Tcapture = 2^(24 − (FREQ >> 4)) master clocks

At capture, j = 0..7, age = clocks since last burst:
prior = age < 4*j ? −16 : 0
offset = prior − 7 − j + (j >= 6 ? 16 : 0)
code ← (code << 1) | (shift(state, offset) & 1)
AM = code XOR 255
PM = AM >= 128 ? 256−AM : −AM

shift advances the recurrence by the specified count, or reverses it for negative offsets. This is an equivalent sampling model, not reconstructed wiring. The random model does not implement the low four FREQ bits. PM endpoints, reset seed (currently 1), and write boundaries remain unresolved. During hold, capture stops while the sequence continues.

7. Implementation limits

AreaCurrent treatment
FREQ writePreserve position/order; restart divider. Exact acceptance clock unknown.
HoldPeriodic position forced to zero; divider/order frozen. Provisional boundary policy.
Wave changePreserve shared position; triangle advances twice. Odd positions interpolated.
PM → pitchq×100/64 cents is approximate; calibrated-table errors are not core errors.
RandomSteady sequence supported; seed, low FREQ bits, boundaries and PM endpoints unresolved.

An independently written equivalent model can be implemented while retaining these limits. Measurement agreement alone does not establish licensing or erase prior reference history. This report changes neither code nor license.

The code source is the pre-rename 0.11b archive. The ZIP hash below identifies that baseline, not the revised archive. No byte identity with the license notices in 0.10b is claimed; that historical validation statement has been corrected.
